options.A: A) It improves readability but reduces performance
options.B: B) It makes code less reusable

Which of the following best describes a pure function?

options.A: A) A function that modifies its input parameters
options.B: B) A function that always returns the same output for the same input and causes no side effects
options.C: C) A function that uses global variables
options.D: D) A function that depends on user input

mcq.answer_text: B) A function that always returns the same output for the same input and causes no side effects

sq.q: Why are pure functions preferred in parallel or multi-user environments?
answer: Pure functions don’t rely on or change external state, avoiding conflicts during execution. This makes them safer and more efficient in multi-threaded or distributed systems. They also enhance reproducibility and make debugging easier.

sq.q: A student record system filters only passed students. How can filter() and pure functions help?
answer: filter() can be used with a pure lambda like lambda x: x['marks'] > 50 . It returns only those records that satisfy the condition without modifying the original data. This ensures data immutability and reusability across different program parts.
